status: Monte Carlo preparation only; no distributions, probabilities or confidence levels assigned
user_direction: Use ranges for unclear inputs and tune through Monte Carlo; distinguish assumption ranges from statistical confidence intervals.

parameters.name: Whole-market populations
parameters.rule: Choose coherent diagnosed/treated totals; derive prevention and untreated residuals; enforce treated<=diagnosed and oral<=totalLTP. No separate independent sampling of resulting segment counts.

parameters.name: Historical first-year/prevalent retention
parameters.rule: For each sampled retention pair, re-solve entries against historical stock. Do not independently draw fitted historical entries.

parameters.name: PHVS first-year retention
parameters.rule: Draw the improvement fraction once; derive retention. Clinical cause share is a French cross-cohort proxy. Shared efficacy/tolerability beliefs may also affect acquisition; correlation unknown, scenario-test rather than invent.

parameters.name: Relative acquisition
parameters.type: Analyst stress grid, not empirical confidence bounds
parameters.rule: Applied to conditional historical state entries; not total market capture or newRx. Separate from future origin-specific capture model.

parameters.name: Payment transitions
parameters.rule: Choose opening/entry paid assumptions; fit one-way conversion only if feasible. Infeasibility rejects that simplified specification, not the observed data. Do not treat equal scenario weights as probability.

reported_intervals: Label future Monte Carlo percentiles model-implied uncertainty intervals conditional on inputs. Reserve statistical confidence intervals for supported sampling models.

demographics.status: Detailed demographic approach superseded by user direction2026-10-08
demographics.rule: Do not also add separate new diagnosis or death flows; no sampling confidence claimed.

XR_first_year_module.rule: Bundled cautious/working/optimistic cases are not probabilities; one-variable sweeps separate acquisition, conversion, delay and retention. Do not automatically draw all independently for MonteCarlo.
XR_first_year_module.dependence: Origin rates share prescriber reach/competitive positioning; worse access may lower conversion and lengthen delay; do not compound pre-paid dropout twice. Retention begins first paid fill here.

multiyear_ramp.rule: Cases are not confidence bounds. Preserve shared population, within-origin overlap, pricing/access dependencies and first-year supply budget. Check IR retention and dose intensity independently. No reapplication of redosing haircut to observed dispensing.
